issues.description: The problem statement explicitly requires initializing the ArrayList of animals in a constructor with no arguments (a no-arg constructor). The solution implementation of Farm only provides a constructor with an int parameter (Farm(int initialCapacity)) and does not provide the required no-arg constructor. This mismatch can confuse students about which constructor to implement and may cause tests or starter code that expect new Farm() to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a public no-argument constructor for Farm that initializes the animals list (e.g. public Farm() { this.animals = new ArrayList<>(); }). Alternatively, if the parameterized constructor is intended, update the problem statement and template to indicate that Farm should have a constructor taking an initial capacity or provide both constructors to satisfy both usages.
